body: I'm not sure that means they're completely hidden from the API, though. Things like autocompletion may recommend them, the Node dock may display them. GDExtension may have them exposed anyway, though the leading underscore is a deterrent.

```suggestion
			code_editor->refactor_request(ScriptLanguage::RefactorKind::REFACTOR_KIND_RENAME);
```
The CodeEditor's `_refactor_request` can just be made public and called directly. I don't see why this would need to go through CodeEdit.
The virtual method, signal, and enum in CodeEdit can then be removed.

body:
I also don't think it needs to be exposed. 
This function (and `get_word_at_pos`) is only for getting symbols for lookup, since it takes into account strings with paths and determines word boundaries differently than the other TextEdit methods. So it is functionally different than `get_word_under_caret` too.
Maybe we should even deprecate `get_word_at_pos`, since it shouldn't really be in TextEdit.

Is there a reason that this isn't a Popup / PopupPanel?
The functionality is similar and it should be on top, so it doesn't get cut off:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f25d84f-162e-4d57-ac81-a4db7e4bcdde)
Oh, I need to take a look at this. I first tried with a popup, but I had issues. But maybe this bug outweighs the other issues I had.

body: Removed it following @kitbdev's changes in the codebase.
See just on top, the lines about EDIT_COMPLETE. I replicated the behavior of code completion.

Note to myself in order to remove the commented diff after testing.
The base behavior changed, but may not be enough without my additional code.

@vnen I replaced the old static char array for keywords with `static const LocalVector<String>` instead. (the declaration is [here](https://github.com/adamscott/godot/blob/c6700a52425987654b13f7c8bc52d84f4e3f402b/modules/gdscript/gdscript_editor.cpp#L1525-L1575)).

Ah, I remember. If it's a popup, it doesn't follow the code scrolling. I think the box following its source is really important.

I'll try though to calculate the position of the fake popup better.

Found a new issue while modifying an Enum value by referring to it by its outside classes (i.e. refactoring `ENUM_VALUE_1` from `InnerInnerB.EnumOfInnerInnerB.ENUM_VALUE_1`)

This is due to that code here.

CodeEdit has functionality for code completion, it draws and maintains the options and provides methods, settings, virtual methods, etc for it. Compared to this, CodeEdit has nothing to do with refactoring and it doesn't need to either. So I still think we should not affect CodeEdit if we can help it, especially if it means exposing a signal.
